claims.text: Applying an approximately 0.5 T magnetic field during thermomechanical processing of MnNiSi-based material will refine its martensitic microstructure.
Applying an approximately 0.5 T magnetic field during thermomechanical processing of MnNiSi-based material will promote twin martensite formation.
The proposed magnetic-field-assisted processing will improve the strength of MnNiSi-based material.
The proposed magnetic-field-assisted processing will improve the ductility of MnNiSi-based material.
The proposed magnetic-field-assisted processing will retain a large magnetocaloric effect in MnNiSi-based material.
Conventionally processed MnNiSi-based magnetocaloric material has a multiphase or unrefined martensitic structure.
Conventionally processed MnNiSi-based magnetocaloric material has moderate mechanical properties.
Conventionally processed MnNiSi-based magnetocaloric material exhibits a large magnetocaloric entropy change.
Processing near the martensitic transformation temperature under controlled thermal conditions allows atomic diffusion and twin martensite formation.
A field around 0.5 T will promote a homogeneous single-phase twin structure in MnNiSi-based material.
The resulting martensitic microstructure will have fewer grain-boundary defects.
The applied magnetic field during thermomechanical processing assists atomic diffusion.
The applied magnetic field energetically favors twin martensite formation.
A homogeneous, defect-reduced twin-martensitic microstructure increases both ductility and strength.
The intrinsic magnetostructural transition responsible for the magnetocaloric effect will be preserved during the proposed processing.
Magnetically processed MnNiSi-based material will have a magnetocaloric entropy change comparable to or greater than material processed without a field.
The expected improvement is limited to a moderate-field regime near 0.5 T.
Fields above the proposed regime or processing outside the optimal temperature range may disrupt the phase transition and reduce the magnetocaloric effect.
